bookCredit: Number the Stars (Lois Lowry, 1989), Freedom Train (Dorothy Sterling, 1954) and Prince Caspian (C. S. Lewis, 1951) are quoted only in short lines. Anne of Green Gables (L. M. Montgomery, 1908) is in the public domain.
title: Two Books, One Shelf

banner.alt: A warm library at golden hour, tall shelves of books, a reading lamp, and an owl perched on the top shelf

keepsake.name: owl feather
keepsake.line: Only Imagination Trip travelers earn this one. Opti left it between your two books.

postcard.h: Ask both books the same question
body: You chose a theme last time. Today you need the same question for two books, and one moment from each that answers it.
Build a shelf: two books, one object from each.
postcard.word: A theme is the big idea about life that a story keeps showing.

mission.p: Two books side by side, one object in front of each, both answering the same question.

steps.build:
Open your menu (top button, right controller) and click Models. Build in this order:
  1. two books on a shelf, one for each novel
  2. in front of book 1: an object from a moment that shows your theme
  3. in front of book 2: an object from the other book’s moment
Only objects from the list, only chapters you have read.
steps.say: Stand in front of your shelf. Practice these 2 sentences:
steps.frame: “In ___, ___ shows ___ when ___. In ___, ___ shows it when ___.”
steps.extra: Perch a Barn Owl on the shelf. That is me, watching your comparison.

points: Your video is 30 seconds or less, shows two books with one object in front of each, and you say 2 sentences: your theme and one moment from each book that shows it, naming the character each time.

alt.p: Five questions about comparing this year’s books. Pick the answer that fits.

qs.q: Which moment shows courage that does not look brave?
opts: Annemarie giggling like Kirsti while soldiers search her basket
Peter drawing his sword in the treasure chamber
Harriet building a carriage from the junk heap
qs.why: Number the Stars, Ch. 15: acting silly is how she keeps the packet safe.

qs.q: Harriet going back for her parents, who are past eighty, is most like which moment?
opts: Caspian riding away from the castle alone
Mama taking the girls to Uncle Henrik’s by herself
qs.why: Both are grown-ups taking the danger on themselves for family. Same question, same shape of answer.

qs.q: Which moment shows a leader admitting a mistake?
opts: Peter kneeling to Aslan and saying he led them wrong
Trumpkin refusing to believe in lions
qs.why: Prince Caspian, Ch. 11: the High King says he is so glad, and so sorry.

qs.q: Which moment shows holding on to what you believe when others doubt?
opts: Trufflehunter saying beasts do not change, they hold on
Nikabrik putting a hand on his dagger
qs.why: Prince Caspian, Ch. 5: the Badger believes in the old kings as firmly as in Aslan.

qs.q: Which pair is a true comparison?
opts: Annemarie risks the soldiers’ dogs; Harriet makes me feel brave
Annemarie risks the soldiers on the path; Harriet risks the road north alone
Anne renames the Avenue; Harriet sings a song
qs.why: Same question for both: what does this character risk? Both answers are moments, not feelings.

alt.miss: Not that one. Ask the same question of both books; each answer must be a moment.

write.q: Name your theme and your two characters. In 2 sentences, give one moment from each book that shows the theme, naming the character each time.

scripts.brief: Hoo there, it’s Opti. You picked a theme last time. Today you need the same question for two books, and one moment from each that answers it. In the library, build a shelf with your two books and set one object in front of each, an object from the moment that shows your theme. Then stand back and tell me the two moments, with the character named each time.
scripts.alt: No headset? Pull up a library chair with me. Comparing means asking both books the same question and getting the same shape of answer. Five questions, one at a time, and every moment comes from a chapter you have read.
scripts.saved: Two books, two objects, one theme. I left an owl feather on the shelf between them. Keep it, and remember that the same big idea can live in two very different stories.

testPara: In Number the Stars, Annemarie shows courage when she carries the basket past the soldiers. In Freedom Train, Harriet shows it too when she leaves the plantation alone at night.
